name: showreel-t01-passkeys

voice.text: Can a fake login page steal your [passkey](/pˈæskˌi/)? No. A password works on any page you type it into. So a lookalike just takes it. A [passkey](/pˈæskˌi/) only works on the site it was made for. On a fake address, there's nothing to give. Turn [passkeys](/pˈæskˌiz/) on.

caption:
Can a fake login page steal your passkey? 🔑

No. A password works on any page you type it into, so a lookalike site (one wrong letter in the address) simply keeps it. A passkey is tied to the site it was made for: on a fake address your phone or browser has nothing to offer, and the real site only ever stores a public key. Turn passkeys on wherever your bank, email and apps offer them.
Send this to someone who still uses one password everywhere.

sources.note: W3C Web Authentication spec source: the RP ID determines the set of origins on which the credential may be exercised; the private key is never exposed; the site receives only the public key
